questions: Did this abnormal appearance or difficulty moving your eyes begin suddenly?
Do you have any loss or blurring of vision?
Do you have eye pain, especially pain when moving your eyes?
Do you have a severe headache, nausea, or vomiting?
Have you noticed that one or both eyes are bulging forward?
Have you had redness, swelling, or discharge from either eye?
Have you had a recent injury or surgery involving your head, face, or eyes?
Have you ever been diagnosed with thyroid disease?
Have you recently had weight loss, heat intolerance, sweating, tremor, or a racing heartbeat?
Have you had weakness, numbness, difficulty speaking, difficulty swallowing, or drooping of the eyelids?
Do you have diabetes, high blood pressure, or any other major medical condition?
Have you recently had an infection, particularly of the sinuses or around the eyes?
Are you taking any medicines, including steroids or thyroid medication?
Have you had similar eye problems before?

results: 1. Measure visual acuity, color vision, and confrontational visual fields in each eye.
visual fields (perimetry): FULL - no bitemporal hemianopia, so no chiasmal compression
2. Examine the pupils for size, reactivity, and a relative afferent pupillary defect.
pupil size and light reaction: equal and reactive
3. Perform ocular motility testing in all positions of gaze, including saccades and smooth pursuit.
smooth pursuit and saccades: normal
vertical gaze and convergence: normal
4. Perform cover–uncover and alternate-cover testing at distance and near.
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
5. Examine for ptosis and fatigability during sustained upgaze and repeated eyelid closure.
ptosis / lid position: none
6. Perform a complete cranial-nerve and neurologic examination, including gait and coordination.
cranial nerve examination: left eye adduction paresis with dissociated abducting paresis of the right eye on rightward gaze; see-saw nystagmus
mental status / cognitive screen: normal
muscle tone examination: normal
limb strength (MRC) examination: normal
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
posture and pull test: normal
gait and tandem walking: normal
7. Measure blood pressure, pulse, temperature, and capillary blood glucose.
blood glucose and HbA1c: fasting glucose 10.88 mmol/L; HbA1c 9%
glucose / HbA1c: fasting glucose 10.88 mmol/L (ref 3.89-6.11) and HbA1c 9% (ref 4-6) - uncontrolled diabetes
8. Obtain an urgent MRI of the brain and orbits with diffusion-weighted imaging and contrast, including the brainstem.
MRI brain with gadolinium: bilateral dorsomedial pontine and left thalamic infarction
MRI diffusion-weighted sequences: restricted diffusion in the bilateral dorsomedial pons and left thalamus
MRI brain with DWI: bilateral dorsomedial PONTINE and LEFT THALAMIC infarction
MRI sella and orbits: normal - no parasellar or suprasellar mass
9. Obtain MR angiography of the head and neck.
CT / MR angiography (posterior circulation): slender left anterior cerebral artery and stenosis of the ipsilateral posterior cerebral artery
CT / MR angiography (circle of Willis): normal / non-contributory
10. Obtain a 12-lead electrocardiogram and cardiac rhythm monitoring.
not performed / not available
11. Measure serum acetylcholine-receptor antibodies and MuSK antibodies.
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: negative
12. Measure TSH and free T4.
TSH / free T4: normal
13. Obtain a complete blood count, electrolytes, renal function, glucose, HbA1c, and lipid profile.
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
blood glucose and HbA1c: fasting glucose 10.88 mmol/L; HbA1c 9%
full blood count and biochemistry: normal
glucose / HbA1c: fasting glucose 10.88 mmol/L (ref 3.89-6.11) and HbA1c 9% (ref 4-6) - uncontrolled diabetes
lipids and vascular risk assessment: normal
14. Perform repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fiber electromyography of the extraocular or facial muscles.
repetitive nerve stimulation: normal
single-fibre electromyography: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acute bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia (WEBINO-type ocular motility disorder) with see-saw nystagmus due to bilateral dorsomedial pontine ischemic infarction, likely diabetic small-vessel cerebrovascular disease

ALTERNATIVE 1: Posterior-circulation embolic ischemic stroke involving the medial longitudinal fasciculi

ALTERNATIVE 2: Multiple sclerosis or other inflammatory demyelinating brainstem disease

ALTERNATIVE 3: Ocular myasthenia gravis
